label: rare reset spike on input c or v early in the original or copy phase
explanation: Extremely sparse unit (about 0.03% of steps). About 91% of activations, holding about 94% of the mass, fall on steps where the input token is c (about 50% of mass) or v (about 44%). A and u make up most of the rest. Firing is confined to early positions: original-phase steps t=2..5, or the first copy steps (recall_idx 1-2, so the fed-back input is orig(0) or orig(1)). It never fires at t=0/1, at the delimiter, or late in either phase. The token and position are necessary but far from sufficient: only about 1% of c/v steps in those windows fire. Context helps some (previous token a/c/w, earlier a/o/w seen; first token o/v/x), but no simple history rule pushes precision above about 5%. Which c/v steps fire seems to depend on a specific hidden-state configuration that the available variables do not capture. Magnitude is small (max 0.03). The largest activations are c at t=3 after a/w-containing prefixes and v at recall_idx 1-2. I did not find a clean magnitude modulator.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: in_tok=v (+4.94), prev_tok=a (+3.75), prev_tok=c (+3.18), in_tok=u (+2.74), prev2_tok=a (+2.58), prev_tok=w (+2.53). Lower it: prev2_tok=- (-2.55), orig_idx=-1 (-2.38), t=7 (-2.36), t=6 (-1.71).
